sections.title: Genealogies
sections.description: From Adam to the return from exile

sections.title: David's Reign
sections.description: David's rule, the ark, and temple preparations

events.title: Genealogies from Adam to Israel
events.description: The book of Chronicles opens with an extensive genealogy stretching from Adam through Noah's sons, Abraham's descendants, and Jacob's twelve sons. These genealogies connect Israel's history to the origin of all humanity and demonstrate God's guidance through generations.

events.title: Judah's lineage and David's line
events.description: The tribe of Judah is given a prominent place in the genealogies. The lineage from Perez through Jesse to David and onward to the subsequent kings is carefully documented, underscoring the legitimacy of David's dynasty and God's promises to Judah.
events.year_display: From the Patriarchs to the Exile

events.title: The Genealogies of the Tribes
events.description: The other tribes of Israel have their genealogies recorded: Simeon, Reuben, Gad, Manasseh, Levi, Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Ephraim, and Asher. The cities and service roles of the Levites receive special attention, reflecting the book of Chronicles' focus on temple worship.
events.year_display: From the Patriarchs to the Exile

events.title: Those Who Returned to Jerusalem
events.description: The genealogies conclude with a list of those who settled in Jerusalem after returning from the Babylonian exile. Priests, Levites, gatekeepers, and temple servants are mentioned, and Saul's family tree is repeated as a transition to the account of his downfall.

events.title: The Death of Saul at Mount Gilboa
events.description: The Philistines attack Israel, and Saul's sons fall in battle. Saul is severely wounded and throws himself on his own sword to avoid being dishonored. The Philistines fasten his head in the temple of Dagon. The book of Chronicles explains that Saul died because he was unfaithful to the Lord and sought guidance from one who consulted with the dead.

events.title: David Anointed King over All Israel
events.description: All the tribes of Israel gathered to David in Hebron and anointed him king over all Israel, as the Lord had spoken through Samuel. They acknowledged that David had already led Israel's army under Saul and that the Lord had appointed him as shepherd and ruler over His people.

events.title: David Conquers Jerusalem
events.description: David and all Israel marched up to Jerusalem, which was then called Jebus. The Jebusites claimed that David could not enter, but Joab was the first to storm the fortress and thus became commander of the army. David settled in the stronghold and called it the City of David, and the city was built around it.

events.title: David's Mighty Men
events.description: A detailed list of David's mighty warriors is presented: the three foremost heroes, the thirty, and the many brave men who joined him. Their deeds are described, from standing alone against Philistine armies to fetching water from Bethlehem's well behind enemy lines. The warriors who came to David in Ziklag and Hebron are also mentioned.

events.title: First attempt to move the ark
events.description: David gathers all Israel to bring the ark of the covenant from Kiriath-Jearim. They place the ark on a new cart, and Uzzah and Ahio drive it. But when the oxen stumble, Uzzah reaches out to steady the ark, and the Lord's anger strikes him down so that he dies. David becomes afraid and leaves the ark at the house of Obed-Edom instead.

events.title: The ark is brought to Jerusalem
events.description: After three months in the house of Obed-Edom, David brings the ark to Jerusalem in the proper way: the Levites carry it on poles as Moses had commanded. David dances with all his might before the Lord, wearing a linen ephod. The ark is placed in the tent David has pitched, and he organizes worship led by Asaph and his brothers.

events.title: God's covenant with David
events.description: David wants to build a house for the Lord, but the prophet Nathan brings God's answer: It is not David who will build a house for God, but God who will build a house for David. The Lord promises that David's son will build the temple and that David's throne will be established forever. David responds with a humble and grateful prayer.

events.title: David's Military Victories
events.description: David leads a series of victorious campaigns: he defeats the Philistines, subdues Moab, overcomes Hadadezer king of Zobah and the Arameans from Damascus. He also conquers the Ammonites and their mercenaries after his envoys are humiliated. Finally, David's men fight bravely among the Philistines. The Lord gives David victory wherever he goes.

events.title: The Census and the Plague
events.description: Satan incites David to take a census of Israel. Joab warns against it, but David insists. The census reveals 1,100,000 fighting men in Israel and 470,000 in Judah. God punishes the people with a plague, and 70,000 die. David sees the Lord's angel with a drawn sword over Jerusalem and buys Araunah's threshing floor, where he builds an altar and offers sacrifices. The Lord answers with fire from heaven.

events.title: Preparations for the Temple
events.description: David declares that Araunah's threshing floor will become the site of the Lord's house. He gathers enormous amounts of materials: gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone. He entrusts Solomon with the task of building the temple and urges him to be courageous and faithful. David also commands all Israel's leaders to help Solomon with this great work.

events.title: The Levitical Service is Organized
events.description: David organizes the roles of the Levites in detail: they are divided into groups for service in the temple, as singers and musicians under Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, as gatekeepers, and as treasurers. The priests are also divided into 24 shifts according to the lines of Zadok and Abiathar. This arrangement lays the foundation for temple service for generations to come.

events.title: David's Farewell Address
events.description: David gathers all the leaders of Israel and delivers his farewell address. He hands over the building plans for the temple to Solomon, drawings he received by the Spirit of the Lord. David generously gives from his personal wealth and encourages the people to do the same. The people give willingly and with joy. David praises the Lord in the hearing of the entire assembly and reminds them that everything belongs to God.

events.title: Solomon Appointed and David's Death
events.description: Solomon is anointed king for a second time, now in full public view, and all Israel acknowledges him. All the leaders and David's sons submit to the new king. David dies after reigning for forty years – seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem. He dies old and full of days, rich in honor and wealth.
